text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGED: Observability ingest failures in eu-west-1 — CloudWatch Logs PutLogEvents throttling. Symptoms: elevated 5xx and tail latency across Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/observability-ingest

observability-bot: alert: cw-logs-put-failures_eu-west-1 fired (90% of forwarder hosts reporting 429/5xx on PutLogEvents). metric: log_forwarder.put_errors.count = 820 in last 10m. sample log: `{"error":"ThrottlingException","message":"Rate exceeded","region":"eu-west-1","service":"logs"}`

dani (oncall): seeing increased 5xx spike on the public API around 14:02 UTC, pages from customers. Confirming impact window. @alice @ben can you triage?

alice (sre): on it. attaching quick grep from forwarder logs showing repeated 429s and retries: ```2026-03-15T14:01:23Z forwarder-12 PUT / PutLogEvents -> 429 ThrottlingException attempt=1 backoff=200ms
2026-03-15T14:01:24Z forwarder-07 PUT / PutLogEvents -> 429 ThrottlingException attempt=2 backoff=400ms
2026-03-15T14:02:01Z forwarder-03 PutLogEvents -> 5xx InternalError (upstream)
``` All errors originate from cw logs ingest in eu-west-1. This correlates with CW API throttles, not our consumer crash.

ben (infra): possible cause: increased CloudWatch Logs PUT rate from our cross-account log-forwarder after a config roll a few hours ago (bigger batch size). We should reduce write concurrency/batch size or route to backup S3 Firehose. Two quick levers: 1) flip feature flag to reduce forwarder batch_size (runtime) 2) enable s3-fallback delivery for failing batches.

carol (prod): customer reports coming in: some Hosted API customers seeing elevated latency and intermittent 5xx. Dedicated pools: higher tail latency, a few calls retried by client libs. Need status page update and support note ready.

frank (support): compiling impacted customers list: customer-tiers A,B,C. will DM PII list to eng. prepping canned reply.

alice (sre): mitigation plan (quick):
- reduce forwarder batch_size to 25 (from 200) and cap concurrency to 4 per-host
- enable s3-backup for Firehose (buffer and de-dupe later)
- increase SDK retry/backoff (from 4 -> 8 retries, exponential base 300ms)
- open AWS support case and request temporary burst limit raise for PutLogEvents in eu-west-1

alice (sre): command to flip feature flag via internal admin API:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/feature/forwarder.batch" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"value":25}'
``` will deploy to all forwarders via config-service.

dani (oncall): executing flag flip now. will monitor. @ben can you stand by to enable s3-fallback if flips don't reduce errors.

ben (infra): standing by. also preparing Kinesis->S3 route in case Firehose can't accept more.

observability-bot: config-change detected: feature forwarder.batch updated to 25 by dani (oncall) at 2026-03-15T14:05:12Z.

alice (sre): seeing immediate drop in PutLogEvents rate, but some hosts still hitting throttles due to retries. patching retry policy now.

alice (sre): applied retry config (env var) on forwarders: ```LOG_FW_MAX_RETRIES=8 LOG_FW_BACKOFF_BASE_MS=300``` restart rolling.

observability-bot: forwarder.error_rate_eu-west-1 decreased from 90% -> 28% in 7m after actions. overall API 5xx rate decreased but tail latency still elevated.

dani (oncall): good. preparing status page update. short summary: "We’re seeing elevated error rates and latency for requests served from eu-west-1 due to CloudWatch Logs ingestion throttling. We’ve applied mitigations to reduce logging load and are routing failed batches to durable fallback. Some customers may have seen increased latency or intermittent 5xx between 14:00–14:10 UTC." publish when ready?

carol (prod): please include customer guidance: no action required; some logs may be delayed. we’ll follow up when full restore confirmed.

frank (support): posting canned reply to customers and linking status page.

alice (sre): opened AWS support case: case 1234567890 (requesting temporary PutLogEvents burst allowance + explanation of spike). shared debug bundle.

erik (eng-ml): any impact to model-serving caches or evictions due to delayed observability? trying to see if KV cache thrash correlates with the same window — preliminary: no correlation. model inference infra looks stable.

ben (infra): we enabled s3-fallback at 14:12 UTC for persistent retries. that took a few hosts out of the hot loop. still watching for residual 5xx.

observability-bot: note: metrics pipeline ingestion (prometheus -> longterm) unaffected; only CloudWatch Logs forwarder path impacted.

dani (oncall): handing to alice for next shift at 14:45 UTC for mitigation follow-through and postmortem. @alice you own doc and next steps?

alice (sre): will own post-incident: assign action items: 1) permanent reduction of forwarder batch defaults + smarter backoff (owner: infra/ben) 2) add cross-region redundancy for log ingestion (owner: infra/ben) 3) refine alert thresholds to include PutLogEvents 429 spikes (owner: observability/erik) 4) customer comms review (owner: product/carol).

frank (support): support follow-up scheduled, will send list of impacted tenants and sample traces.

aws-support: AWS case 1234567890: requested throughput increase; AWS responded: "We see throttling due to account-level spike. We can temporarily increase for 1 hour while you implement mitigations. Please confirm desired increase and timeframe."

carol (prod): confirmed temporary increase for 1 hour while we finish fallback tasks. thanks.

dani (oncall): wrap-up: incident degraded at 14:25 UTC, mitigations reduced error rate and improved latency; customer impact limited to delayed logs and some increased tail latency/5xx for a small subset. handing to alice for postmortem and RCA.

alice (sre): note for postmortem: timeline, config roll that increased batch size earlier today, lack of automatic cross-region fallback, and need for softer default cluster-wide settings. will draft and share within 72h. tagging owners in doc.

frank (support): marking customers notified. closing support loop after postmortem.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. postmortem owner: alice (sre). severity: Sev3.

carol (prod): thanks team. good quick coordination. :thumbsup:

alice (sre): handing to Ben for infrastructure follow-up at 15:00 UTC. handing complete.

ben (infra): ack. will schedule change to batch defaults and start design for cross-region ingestion.

--- end thread ---
